He soon learned why it is dangerous to deal with a devil for Beatriz was by his side, but as a nun, even farther from his grasp. Feeling betrayed by both god and devil a like, he swore he wouldn't lose his soul without reason and constructed a suit of brass which had the power to conceal the soul of whomever wore it. However, it required the blood of an innocent woman to seal it, ensuring the security of his soul. The Bishop turned to the only woman whose soul he could entrust was pure, that of Beatriz. When Mephisto noticed the Bishop's soul was missing, he sent out one of his demons, Dargil, to investigate. But the Bishop had been waiting and beheaded him, putting his head on a chain as his servant. He then challenged Mephisto to return his soul, but Mephisto would only give it back to him in exchange for Beatriz, which was in heaven. The Brass Bishop vowed he would never trade her soul for his but as the years passed, he grew more weary of life and decided to capture Beatriz' soul to hand over to Mephisto. To that end he built the mystical Tower of Babel which would lead to heaven, through the use of the Solomon Seal. However, Puck and the sorcerer Modred were able to stop him. The Brass Bishop re-surfaced however, and took over the town of White Cross, Newfoundland, where he reconstructed the Tower using the citizens as slaves. Alpha Flight was sent in to investigate. While Puck's memories of his encounter with the Bishop were clouded, he soon remembered all. The Bishop had attempted to lure Puck out so that he could use him as a pathfinder to the Solomon Seal. Which he did, after gaining control of him in the Tower. But Puck was able to gain enough control over himself (with the help of the other souls the Bishop had trapped) to to use the Solomon Seal (which mystically opens anything) to unseal the brass armour. Standing feet away from the gates to heaven, the armour came undone and Mephisto welcomed Benedico de Vica Severtes to his immortal realm. The Bishop gone, the Tower disappeared and the townspeople returned to normal. Powers: The Bishop had no super-natural powers save for limited mystical knowledge and abilities. After the Torch defeated the Syndicate's leader the so-called Crime Boss, Chief Wilson was informed of that the Crime Boss was responsible for the Torch's disappearance back in '49. After the Torch rescued his partner Toro from Communist agents in Korea, the Torch was informed that a Communist spy called the Butcher had kidnapped the Chief's daughter Mary in retaliation of the Torch's recent activities and had demanded the Torch's surrender in exchange for Mary's freedom. The Torch and Toro ended up rescuing Mary and slaying the Butcher, and the pair decided to resume their crime fighting career. Chief Wilson became their closest ally and he frequently assisted the flaming duo on their cases throughout the 1950s, acting as a liaison between the heroes and various levels of law enforcement and government agencies and providing the resources of his office to the crime fighting duo. After being installed as President, Dominguez held and won democratic elections. Dominguez worked from the Presidential Palace of the country, in the capital city Ciudad Leando. He was married to Carmilla Dominguez, who had access to his office, and was a friend and associate to Ciudad Leando University professor Hector Silva. With an approach of enlightened despotism, Dominguez failed to solve the problems of an impoverished population. Only a few months after the election, General Emmanuel Rodrigo Raposa gathered the poorest social classes in Bosqueverde and led them in a socialist uprising against Dominguez, the "Raposistas", with promises of democratic reforms. Raposa's army laid siege to Ciudad Leando during summer. Dominguez's wedding anniversary took place during the siege, yet he had little reason to celebrate, knowing that Raposa would likely win the civil war. Dominguez made a deal with Raposa so that Dominguez would legitimize Raposa as ruler of Bosqueverde, in exchange for one million U.S. dollars in gold krugerrands. Raposa accepted, and Dominguez kept the treasure in a locked strongbox in a wine cellar of the palace; only his wife, who was also in the loop, knew where the money was, or that the key was in Dominguez's office desk. Dominguez and his wife prepared to leave the country with a military escort promised by Raposa, that was to take them to a plane to fly to Europe. However, Raposa decided to betray Dominguez, murder him and recover the money. He sent a group of hired international mercenaries to the Palace, with orders to capture Dominguez alive but Raposa told only the mercenary leader, Broward "Bo" Ollsen, what was his real objective: Kill Dominguez and get the money. After a street-to-street battle, only two mercenaries arrived at Dominguez's office: Ollsen and ex-marine Marc Spector. The President and his wife were there, packing their bags. Mikaboshi is more akin to a force of nature than a physical being, and having existed as a dark, primordial void that once dominated Earth (and before even that, the Prime Universe, and before even that, the several realities predating the Prime Universe itself) in its earliest days, Mikaboshi's true form is elusive. Mikaboshi was able to gather enough power to shed his "Terran form" and emerge as the Chaos King, the primal embodiment of nothingness and primordial chaos that served as a natural opposing power to both Eternity and Death, and a threat to the entire multiverse and all of its super-powered mortals, living or dead, its abstract conceptual beings, its cosmic beings and its lesser divinities. Origin Amatsu-Mikaboshi (Earth-616) Origin The entity known as Amatsu-Mikaboshi originated as an aspect of Oblivion, the abstract entity embodying the void that existed before the universe even began. An incarnation of the primordial darkness and chaos that existed before the universe, the Chaos King existed as a dark counterpart to Eternity, whose genesis stripped the Chaos King of much of its power and led to it being integrated into the Shinto cosmology as "Amatsu-Mikaboshi." According to Shinto cosmology, Amatsu-Mikaboshi ruled over the Earth all alone when it was nothing more than a formless void of primordial darkness, until the elder goddess known as Gaea--in the form of Izanami--and a young Amatsu-Kami called Izanagi created the islands of Japan from the Void using the divine Jeweled Spear, and populated it with their divine children the lesser Amatsu-Kami--who later came to be worshipped as gods by the humans of Japan. The dark god was enraged that his void was now gone and wasn't the only being in existence anymore, and so he declared war on Izanami, Izanagi, and the Amatsu-Kami. He was ultimately imprisoned in the netherworld of Yomi, where he remained for centuries, which he spent accruing an army of oni, shinma demons, and other evil spirits and monsters inhabiting the underworld. Recovering a sample of Atom Water from one of the dead soldiers, Cap turned it over to the military where he was informed America had developed a more powerful weapon: The Atom Bomb. served: Dar-Benn (Earth-616) Dar-Benn (Earth-616) Dar-Benn (Earth-616) Dar-Benn (Earth-616) Type: character Name: Dar-Benn Gender: Male Origin: Kree Reality: Earth-616 Place of Death: Kree-Lar Cause of Death: Killed by Cal'syee Neramani Killedby: Cal'syee Neramani (Earth-616) Identity: No Dual Citizenship: Kree Empire Occupation: Formerly: Joint-Emperor of the Kree Empire Base of Operations: Kree-Lar, Pama System Creators: Ron Marz; Ron Lim First: Silver Surfer Vol 3 53 Death: Avengers Vol 1 346 Overview: Dar-Benn is a Kree general who rose through the military ranks of the Kree Empire. Alongside General Ael-Dan, he orchestrated a coup against Emperor Clumsy Foulup by commissioning a robotic duplicate of the Silver Surfer to assassinate the Emperor and his advisor during a live broadcast, blaming the attack on the Skrulls. After seizing power as co-rulers, Dar-Benn and Ael-Dan pursued aggressive expansionist policies, defunding key scientific projects and escalating the Kree war with the Shi'ar Imperium. They imposed martial law and sought to consolidate control amid the Empire's ongoing crises. Their reign ended abruptly when Deathbird publicly assassinated both generals during a confrontation with the Avengers and a rogue Kree militia. Following their deaths, their preserved neural patterns were absorbed into the Supreme Intelligence's collective consciousness, further strengthening its influence over the Kree Empire. History: ===Early Life=== Dar-Benn was born on Kree-Lar a planet in the heart of the Kree Empire. From a young age, both showed exceptional dedication to the military traditions of the Kree Empire. They joined the Kree military at an early stage in their lives, steadily rising through the ranks due to their strategic acumen and combat prowess. Their careers set the foundation for their eventual leadership roles within the Kree military hierarchy. ===Conspiracy Against Emperor Clumsy Foulup=== In the aftermath of extensive military funding cuts imposed by the Kree Emperor known as Clumsy Foulup, two prominent Kree generals, Ael-Dan and Dar-Benn, grew increasingly dissatisfied with his leadership. Viewing the Emperor's greed and fiscal negligence as a threat to the stability of the Empire, they secretly conspired to remove him from power and install themselves as joint rulers. To execute their plan, Ael-Dan and Dar-Benn commissioned Dr. Kaer-Linn, an advanced robotics specialist, to construct a highly realistic robotic duplicate of the Silver Surfer, intended to act as their weapon during the assassination. During their drive, Anna Marie reflected on how when she was young, she believed that her parents had been taken away by aliens, when in reality they had passed away. This made the idea of Touch being from another planet a little more palatable. She began questioning him on the logistics of his travels such as how he could understand English, to which he responded by pulling out his translator orb. He also admitted that his name was not really James but that it was unpronounceable in English since it was a name composed of mostly whistles in a sing-songy tune that actually translated to the name Touch. As they were driving out of La Porte, Indiana, they felt guilty about the car they had stolen and backtracked to Ohio where they would leave the car and send a note to the owner on where to find it. From there they planned on stealing another car but from a dealership this time. During this time, they also found an ATM machine and Anna Marie learned how Rogue came into possession of so much money. He had been using a blue orb, similar to the translator, to take money out of the ATMs without raising suspicions from the banks. While at the hotel, Anna Marie and Touch's feelings towards each other increased, each desperately wanting to touch the other but being physically incapable of doing so. While the two sat in bed, Touch said he'd refer to Anna Marie as Rogue from now on, on account of her Rogue gene that caused her mutation. She accepted the name as she felt that the version of herself she once knew had stopped existing once she gained her powers. Originally, there was no Multiverse. The First Firmament was a single, eternal, unchanging universe. However, its first beings, the Celestials, shattered it into the first-ever Multiverse, the Second Cosmos. As the Celestials had desired change and evolution, the Multiverse died and was reborn several times, evolving each time. The Third Cosmos introduced narrative; the Fourth, archetypes; the Fifth, magic; and the Sixth, science. In Earth-616's previous incarnation in the Sixth Cosmos, the Paradise-like planet of Taa existed. When the sixth incarnation was destroyed by an entity called the Black Winter, it left an existential void in its wake until the universe was eventually reborn with the Big Bang. The current universe was part of the Seventh Cosmos. It was where Earth existed, protected by super heroes like the Fantastic Four, the Avengers, and the X-Men. However, the Multiverse was destroyed by beings from outside the Multiverse called the Beyonders and the phenomenon known as the incursions. The intervention of Mister Fantastic in the Multiverse's rebirth caused the Eighth Cosmos to be a direct continuation of the Seventh, instead of being a completely new version. Because of the abnormal nature of the most recent death and rebirth of the Multiverse, some cosmic beings argue that it is still the Seventh Cosmos, but slight differences in reality confirm that it is truly the Eighth. Earth-616 was the first universe to be re-created in the Eighth Cosmos, so the Maker considered it the "Prime Universe." ===Seventh and Eighth Incarnations=== Born into the Seventh Cosmos, the universe came into being with the Big Bang, where the Celestials appeared and began creating planets, stars, galaxies, and life itself. The Dark God Knull was selected to be the King in Black by the Celestials, but he declared war on them and all of existence instead. His little brother was saying his final goodbye to him before his demise and was warning him of his “evil self” (Ikol). Odinson infuriated, enacts retribution for Kid Loki’s murder and begins to pummel Ikol. However because the Elder Loki is using the age-acceraleted body of his child self Odinson hesitates to strike further. He instead takes him to Asgard and publically outs him as a copy of the original Loki, Asgard’s greatest enemy and his use of Kid Loki’s body as a vessel. The land was, in some ways, alive, and brought Kevin there to protect it. With his father dead, he was raised by the land, becoming known as Ka-Zar. When he became a man, the land brought him the perfect mate; Shanna O'Hara. Ka-Zar would later encounter the mutant heroes known as the X-Men. He and Shanna would also accidentally free the demon Belasco, the lord of Limbo, from his frozen state. Belasco would kidnap X-Man Illyana Rasputina before being defeated. Early Life Shanna O'Hara (Earth-616) Early Life Shanna O'Hara was the daughter of Gerald O'Hara, a diamond miner who lived and worked in Africa. Born in Zaire (now the "Democratic Republic of the Congo" due to the sliding timescale) she spent most of her youth playing in the jungles. When she was only six, Gerald O'Hara went to kill a leopard that had gone rogue; that leopard had once belonged to Patricia O'Hara, Shanna's mother. Unfortunately, while he was hunting the animal, Gerald accidentally shot and killed Patricia. This event started Shanna's lifelong crusade against guns and other firearms. After the incident, Shanna moved to the United States of America to live with some relatives. She there studied to be a veterinarian at university and also became an accomplished Olympic athlete, specializing in track and field and competitive swimming. After completing her university studies, Shanna was offered work placement as a zoologist at Central Park Municipal Zoo in New York City. While at the zoo, Shanna raised a female leopard she named Julani. But one day, another traumatic incident occurred when Julani was shot and killed by a zoo guard. The next day, the zoo's director asked Shanna to take Julani's cubs, Ina and Biri, to the Dahomey Reserve in Africa. Shanna decided to stay with the animals and, wearing Julani's pelt as an honor, became Shanna, the She-Devil. The animals were tragically killed when the sorcerer Raga-Shah transferred their life forces into the blood beast Ghamola, which Shanna was forced to destroy. served: Heroes of Krakoa Jean Grey (Earth-616) Heroes of Krakoa The nation of Krakoa entered war against its mirror counterpart Arakko on the grounds of Otherworld in a bizarre contest, in which Cable was listed as a participant. Parallel to this, Jean Grey, Cyclops and Cable investigated the ruins of the Peak, S.W.O.R.D.'s former space station whose crew had been exterminated by the extradimensional interlopers called the Vescora. Cable was trapped in Otherworld as Krakoa was at disadvantage in the challenges. In desperation, he contacted Jean Grey to inform her an urgent reaction was needed, otherwise Krakoa would be invaded and consumed by the hellish ghouls of Amenth. This prompted Jean Grey and Cyclops to reform the X-Men, opposing the recommendations of the Quiet Council and costing Grey her position in the government. Aboard the Peak, Jean Grey led an army of X-Men to battle for Krakoa while also instructing Magik to teleport the Vescora to act as cannon fodder. The war ended with Krakoa emerging victorious. Disillusioned with the shadows cast by the Quiet Council, Jean Grey and Cyclops rejected seats offered to them in it. Alternatively, they declared the X-Men should be restructured to act on the behalf of mutants as an independent and free team, chosen and elected by its people. During the Hellfire Gala, a psychic election was held to select the new team. Jean Grey gathered the votes, announcing the new X-Men at Cyclops' side. Based at the Treehouse in Central Park, the X-Men started their operations. Their first crises involved alien incursions, one against the Mind Reaver, during which Jean Grey used her psychic powers to shield the population of Manhattan from its influence, and another by the Annihilation Wave in Kansas, when she combined her powers with the magnetic abilities of Polaris to scan a deceased mind and bring victory to the X-Men. Both had been inflicted by Cordyceps Jones, an extraterrestrial crime-lord, who operated on Gameworld, a casino where aliens gambled on planets. The X-Men eventually infiltrated his installations, with Jean Grey personally confronting Cordyceps Jones and his infectious fungal organism. Jean Grey is the strongest and complete host of Phoenix Force and as such, she is even capable of forcibly ripping it out of another host and forcing its status upon herself. They became the White Phoenix of the Crown and ruled over the omniverse in the white hot room. It was even revealed that Jean Grey is the Phoenix and always is the Phoenix, even when she’s not the Phoenix. And the Phoenix is always Jean, even when it’s not Jean. In 1935, he killed a group of men who made fun of his appearance, an act that landed him on death row and to the electric chair. Somehow surviving, Klug went into seclusion and began developing a massive electrical generator hidden in a cave that charged specially made lightning guns so that he could slay those responsible for sending him to the chair. With the help of his minions, Klug began using his lightning generator to strike the homes of the law officials who were responsible for sending him away. The strange killings attracted the attention of both the Sub-Mariner and Betty Dean. After saving the life of the Governor of New England, Namor triangulated the source of the attacks but was struck down with a bolt of lightning himself. Klug then kidnapped Betty and told her his origins. Deciding that Betty should be his wife, he then hooked her up to his electrical generator, telling her the electricity would deform her and make her uglier than he was. Having survived the electrical jolt, Namor destroyed the hydro-generator that powered Klug's device and defeated his men. Getting hold of an electrical pistol, Namor confronted Klug to a duel. Namor ultimately one, one of his electrical jolts sending Klug falling seemingly to his death. In the aftermath of the battle, Betty noted that Klug was wearing a rubber suit and might still be alive. Namor dismissed this notion and returned to the ocean. As Klug has not been seen since, it is presumable that he is indeed dead. Equipment: Klug had a massive dynamo that recharged his lightning guns. Transportation: Klug rode a motorcycle with a sidecar. Weapons: Klug wielded a lighting gun, which actually shot jolts of electricity that were lethal. They required to be recharged by a massive generator. These weapons could be fired at long ranges as Klug specified that it was these guns that he used to eliminate his targets from afar. Early Life Maxwell Dillon (Earth-616) Early Life Maxwell Dillon was born in Endicott, New York, the son of Jonathan and Anita Dillon. As a child, Max often moved from one town to the next due to his father Jonathan's difficulty in holding down steady employment. One day Jonathan Dillon announced he was running off with another woman and left Anita and Maxwell to fend for themselves. This resulted in Anita becoming overprotective of her son. After Maxwell graduated high school, he announced his plans to go to the university to pursue a degree in electrical engineering. Anita, not wanting her son to become a failure like his father, lied that he was rejected from college. Instead, she suggested he find work at the local electric company, which Maxwell pursued instead, getting a job as a lineman. When Maxwell was 24 years old, his mother had a heart attack and died soon thereafter. Maxwell found a steady job with the electric company, but his income was limited. He soon started dating a woman named Norma Lynn, who was a billing clerk at the electric company, and they eventually married. While Maxwell did not want a woman like his mother, he found the opposite problem in Norma. She complained that she wanted a stable household with a good earner and felt that Maxwell's inability to abandon his lineman's job for greener pastures was a liability. Soon she ran off with an engineer who could provide a life for her that Maxwell could not. The repeat of his parents' failed relationship in his own life caused Maxwell to resolve to find a new woman. However, this would set events in motion that would soon culminate in a criminal career. Dillon resolved to find himself a trophy wife whom he could control with money and would probably not stray as did Norma, lest she be cut off. This mixture of pride and lust added a third deadly sin to Dillon's attitude, greed, and he sought to find any way to stop "treading water" in life. Origins James Howlett (Earth-41578) Origins Born in Canada in 1832, James Howlett was raised by his father John Howlett alongside his half-brother Victor Creed. James was a mutant, but his mutant abilities of regeneration, heightened senses, and retractable bone claws, did not manifest until 1845, after witnessing the death of his father at the hands of Thomas Logan. Grief-stricken and full of rage, James' bone claws came out for the first time and he impaled Thomas with them, fatally wounding him. In his last moments, Thomas revealed that he was actually James' biological father, confusing and frightening James and prompting him to run away with Victor, a fellow mutant with similar powers. James and Victor spent the next several decades operating as soldiers, fighting for the Union in the American Civil War, and later the Allied Forces in World War I and World War II. On August 9, 1945, James was being held captive in a bunker in Nagasaki when the Allies dropped the atomic bomb. James managed to save the life of one Japanese officer, Yashida, and escaped the island to spend some time on his own in the United States, where he worked as a bodyguard in 1973. The Origin James Howlett (Earth-616) The Origin James Howlett's life began in the luxurious Howlett Estate, located in Cold Lake, Alberta, Canada. The notably frail and ill child was born to Elizabeth Howlett, who was married to the mansion's owner John Howlett. However, he was the illegitimate fruit of Elizabeth's affair with the Howletts' groundskeeper, the crass Thomas Logan. Although surrounded by the care of servants and the love of his father John, James was largely neglected by his mother, who had been deeply traumatized following the death of her first son, John Jr.. Around the time Rose O'Hara, a red-headed Irish girl, was admitted work as his companion, he was close to Thomas Logan's mistreated son who was nicknamed "Dog". Originally, there was no Multiverse. The First Firmament was a single, eternal, unchanging universe. However, its first beings, the Celestials, shattered it into the first-ever Multiverse, the Second Cosmos. As the Celestials had desired change and evolution, the Multiverse died and was reborn several times, evolving each time. The Third Cosmos introduced narrative; the Fourth, archetypes; the Fifth, magic; and the Sixth, science. In Earth-616's previous incarnation in the Sixth Cosmos, the Paradise-like planet of Taa existed. When the sixth incarnation was destroyed by an entity called the Black Winter, it left an existential void in its wake until the universe was eventually reborn with the Big Bang. The current universe was part of the Seventh Cosmos. It was where Earth existed, protected by super heroes like the Fantastic Four, the Avengers, and the X-Men. However, the Multiverse was destroyed by beings from outside the Multiverse called the Beyonders and the phenomenon known as the incursions. The intervention of Mister Fantastic in the Multiverse's rebirth caused the Eighth Cosmos to be a direct continuation of the Seventh, instead of being a completely new version. Because of the abnormal nature of the most recent death and rebirth of the Multiverse, some cosmic beings argue that it is still the Seventh Cosmos, but slight differences in reality confirm that it is truly the Eighth. served: Early Years Thaddeus Ross (Earth-616) Early Years Thaddeus E. Ross was born to Alexander and Elizabeth Ross into a New Hampshire family with a rich military heritage. A Ross ancestor fought under General Sherman in the Union Army during the American Civil War, and another was made a general in the Argonne during World War I. Although his grandfather was a farmer and Ross grew up on the family farm in western New Hampshire, his father pursued a career as a professional soldier and his mother was a scientist. As a boy, Thaddeus befriended the neighboring Franklin Storm, and the two spent much of their time playing at war. Because Alexander was away on Army duty for most of Thaddeus' childhood, their neighbor Mr. Garvin effectively became his day-to-day father figure, even beginning an affair with Elizabeth that Thaddeus never learned about. Despite this, Thaddeus idolized his absent father and internalized the Ross ideal of military duty and sacrifice; his father read his son stories of valor when he was home. He received a toy tank for his eighth Christmas that he played with obsessively, and by the age of 10 he had already flown solo for the first time. At the age of 13, he began taking flying lessons in earnest and performed old-fashioned barnstorming shows to help pay for the costs. When Thaddeus was 16, his friend Henry's father borrowed a Mustang fighter plane from the local National Guard station to fly home on leave. The engine stalled over the Ross farm and the plane crashed into nearby woods. Thaddeus, Henry, and their friends reached the wreck in time for Henry to see his father's body still in the cockpit, a trauma that pushed Henry into a breakdown and pushed Thaddeus further toward aviation. Working for a crop duster in the next county, Ross learned more about flying and eventually bought the plane himself. During a summer aerial show, he crashed and was placed in a full body cast, with doctors telling him he would never walk again, a prognosis he ultimately proved wrong. Formerly Los Diablos Missile Base Formerly General Thaddeus "Thunderbolt" Ross Betty Ross Dr. Bruce Banner Rick Jones Captain David Anderson Becoming a Hulk Thaddeus Ross (Earth-199999) Becoming a Hulk Hurt also voiced a variant Thaddeus Ross in the video game . Whereas his comic book counterpart is a lieutenant general in the United States Air Force, Thaddeus Ross of Marvel Cinematic Universe is a lieutenant general in the United States Army. When seen in the film wearing his class A green service uniform, Ross's decorations can be visually recognized as including the Combat Infantryman Badge, Master Parachutist Badge, and Air Assault Badge. However, Ross incorrectly wears the Infantry branch insignia and wears a rack of inauthentic ribbons, none of which are actual US military decorations. served: Early Life Madame Curie Cho (Earth-616) Early Life Madame Curie Cho or Maddy for short is the daughter of Philip Cho and Helen Cho who both hailed from South Korea. She was born in Tucson, Arizona were her parents lived due to her father's job. The Chos lived a normal and happy life, but Amadeus showed from his very childhood that he was different: he was incredibly smart for such a young boy, and learnt a lot of things by himself, becoming highly cultured and increasing his already remarkable intelligence. When her brother was fifteen years old, the Excello, a soap corporation, announced an online game to reward young geniuses, a quiz show named Brain Fight. Amadeus participated, and he easily won the $500,000 reward, placing first. The person who had organized Brain Fight, in fact, was another genius and former child prodigy, Pythagoras Dupree, whose real aim was to search the world for other people whose intellect might rival his own... and to eliminate them as unwanted rivals. By winning his game, Amadeus Cho had been awarded with the title of Mastermind Excello and the position of "7th Smartest Man in the World" (Pythagoras, by his own claim, was the 6th), and that was more than enough a reason to be killed. Dupree had his men attack Amadeus' house, and in the following explosion, his family was killed. Modern Age Hades (Underworld) Modern Age The Olympians went to war with Mikaboshi in his realm of Ama and Hades, the Underworld. Pluto and the Hell-Lords battled Gloriana (Meggan Puceanu) across the respective realm. Amadeus Cho and Hercules during a mission to save Zeus from the Hades, while Hercules battled hordes of vengeful enemies in Tartarus, Amadeus ended up in the Elysian Fields (the Greek version of Heaven), where he met his parents again. Before he could finish apologizing for having "caused" their death by winning Brain Fight, Helen Cho and Philip Cho interrupted him and hugged him, happy and proud of what their son had become. Before he could come back to Earth, however, Helen told Amadeus something he didn't know yet: Maddy didn't die in the explosion, and was still alive, taken by the Excello and kept somewhere, needing his help. She would have watched over her children from the Elysian Fields, but she couldn't have done much else: it was up to Amadeus to make things right, and to reunite what remained of their family. Howlett was sent to and tested on in a remote facility that would later be known as the Weapon X facility, while Fury was sent to New York to join other African American test subjects for an experiment known as Project Rebirth. Early Years James Howlett (Earth-1610) Early Years Later, he awakened inside the Weapon X complex under experimentation by Dr. Abraham Cornelius; who was working for the Canadian government to assist them in their attempts to create their own version of Captain America. James escaped the complex, but was shot as he neared freedom. His wounds miraculously healed and he was recaptured. Cornelius explained that, in their experiments, they accidentally discovered a genome that, when activated, grants the person carrying it various abilities based on their DNA. He called these altered humans "mutants"; and Howlett was dubbed "Mutant Zero". This genome was later released and spread around the world, resulting in the creation of the mutant race. Some time later, the young mutant son of two Weapon X scientists (Erik Lensherr), who was horrified by how James was being treated, killed his parents and set him free. Originally, there was no Multiverse. The First Firmament was a single, eternal, unchanging universe. However, its first beings, the Celestials, shattered it into the first-ever Multiverse, the Second Cosmos. As the Celestials had desired change and evolution, the Multiverse died and was reborn several times, evolving each time. The Third Cosmos introduced narrative; the Fourth, archetypes; the Fifth, magic; and the Sixth, science. In Earth-616's previous incarnation in the Sixth Cosmos, the Paradise-like planet of Taa existed. When the sixth incarnation was destroyed by an entity called the Black Winter, it left an existential void in its wake until the universe was eventually reborn with the Big Bang. The current universe was part of the Seventh Cosmos. It was where Earth existed, protected by super heroes like the Fantastic Four, the Avengers, and the X-Men. However, the Multiverse was destroyed by beings from outside the Multiverse called the Beyonders and the phenomenon known as the incursions. The intervention of Mister Fantastic in the Multiverse's rebirth caused the Eighth Cosmos to be a direct continuation of the Seventh, instead of being a completely new version. Because of the abnormal nature of the most recent death and rebirth of the Multiverse, some cosmic beings argue that it is still the Seventh Cosmos, but slight differences in reality confirm that it is truly the Eighth. served: Origin / Childhood James Howlett (Earth-616)/Expanded History Origin / Childhood Wolverine's life began in Cold Lake, Alberta, Canada, sometime between 1882 and 1885. The mutant who would come to be known simply as "Logan" was born James Howlett, the illegitimate son of Elizabeth Howlett (who was married to John Howlett, owner of a large estate) and the Howletts' grounds-keeper, Thomas Logan. As a boy, James was notably frail and prone to bouts of allergic attacks. He was largely neglected by his mother, who had been institutionalized for a time following the death of her first son, John Jr., in 1897. James was constantly under the pressure of his grandfather, Mr. Howlett, who believed that James required constant punishment by a strong hand, in order to be raised properly. "Firm, but fair," was what Mr. Howlett said to justify his abusive actions. Earth-616 speaker The Maker Earth-616 quotesource Ultimates 2 Vol 2 9 Earth-616 history ===Foreword: The Multiversal Cycle=== All of reality has gone through eight different incarnations, each one triggered by a different instance of multiversal renewal, which constitutes in the destruction and re-creation of everything there is. Originally, there was no Multiverse. The First Firmament was a single, eternal, unchanging universe. However, its first beings, the Celestials, shattered it into the first-ever Multiverse, the Second Cosmos. As the Celestials had desired change and evolution, the Multiverse died and was reborn several times, evolving each time. The Third Cosmos introduced narrative; the Fourth, archetypes; the Fifth, magic; and the Sixth, science. In Earth-616's previous incarnation in the Sixth Cosmos, the Paradise-like planet of Taa existed. When the sixth incarnation was destroyed by an entity called the Black Winter, it left an existential void in its wake until the universe was eventually reborn with the Big Bang. Speaker: Miss Locke Quotesource: Uncanny X-Men Vol 1 145 History: Miss Locke was a devout follower of Arcade and recruited the X-Men to save him when he was kidnapped by Doctor Doom. Once, as a birthday present, she tried to kill him using robots to the likeness of Doctor Doom, giving him a great thrill. Miss Locke was famous because she "never smiled". However, a glimpse of a smile could be seen when she was drugging the X-Men when accepting defeat during the birthday surprise, and again when hearing one of Murderworld's intended victims Courtney Ross telling a joke to survive. Miss Locke and Arcade frequently played games where they attempted to kill each other. Although intended as a sadistic form of fun, they eventually went too far and Arcade murdered Locke in a fit of rage. To hide his crime and use it for his amusement, Arcade staged a complex "Jack the Ripper"-like series of murders, hiding Miss Locke's body among the victims. He also arranged to blame Wolverine for the murders, and recruited Mastermind to help "punish" the mutant killer. The truth was eventually found out and Mastermind left Arcade in a telepathically-induced delusion. Miss Locke has since been seen alive, but whether her death was faked or if Arcade was merely using his lifelike robots to imitate his lost partner is unknown. Arcade would later confirm he did murder Miss Locke in cold blood despite her years of faithful service once she, in Arcade’s mind, had tried to get “too close” to him by having an emotional and physical relationship. After the Mutant Registration Act all mutants were identified at birth and given registration numbers (which were burnt into the forearm) as well as suppression medication that stopped their mutant abilities from manifesting. Beneath the futuristic New York streets, Chad stumbled upon the preserved brain of scientific genius and former superhero Reed Richards, who supplied him with placebo medicine to substitute for the real things, allowing his suppressed mutant abilities to manifest. Together the pair protected the innocent from the few non-mutant threats such as the Mole People or more often from being harmed during the single-minded Sentinel fights with rogue mutants. Reed aided Chad with a cybernetic body built in the form of his former colleague Ben Grimm. ===League of Losers=== Chad was an ally of the "The League of Losers". The league was a group of heroes including Terror, Dagger, Darkhawk, Gravity, Sleepwalker, Speedball, and X-23. They came to the future to prevent the villain Chronok from stealing Richards' time machine, who planned to come to the present and kill all the major heroes. The team defeated Chronok, but they couldn't go back to their present, due to time-travel and alternate timelines. The group decided to stay in the future, satisfied with the impact they made, however unnoticed. Mutant 2099 suggested reforming the Avengers or the "Fantastic Nine". Powers: Chad uses telekinesis to enhance his and above human levels, and can even use it to and in a manner similar to Spider-Man's web-slinging. Equipment: Chad's equipment most notably resembles Spider-Man (although he has no connections to him) with a form fitting blue costume, a full head mask (except for an open-hair top), and insectoid visors on the eyes. Trivia: Chad shares his name with ex-Nirvana drummer Chad Channing, but Kirkman claims this was a coincidence. In the one shot , Chad's registration number is revealed to actually end in 2099 with the beginning of the number remaining obscured by his clothing. He was a businessman rival to Michael Berengetti, owner of the Coliseum Casino, and one of his worst enemies. Although Striker was a criminal and wanted to be the The most powerful man in Las Vegas, did not dare take action directly against Berengetti as long as Berengetti had adequate protection, which included the super-powered enforcer Mr. Fixit; Striker did not know Fixit's name, but he knew that Berengetti was well protected. After Fixit stopped working for Berengetti, Striker hired the superpowered freelance hitman Frost as his main enforcer in the city, yet Striker had many other men at his command. Striker sent Frost to assassinate Berengetti on his orders. The widow, Suzi Berengetti, inherited the Coliseum and other businesses from her husband, but Striker hoped to intimidate her into giving him everything. During her funeral, Striker convinced several Coliseum employees that he was going to be the city's next top man, so that they would let him into Berengetti's private offices, possibly to conduct industrial espionage. His presence there surprised Mrs. Berengetti when she returned with her friend Mona. Striker asked Mrs. Berengetti to hand over her husband's private files and bank accounts, saying that Michael Berengetti would have wanted Striker to keep them. Mrs. Berengetti, who knew Striker, told him to go to hell and insulted him, but Striker saw that she had no one who could protect her and mocked her. Then Berengetti's former protector, Mr. Fixit, arrived, accompanied by his own entourage of thugs, claiming that Fixit, not Striker, was the top man in Las Vegas. Striker sent his goons after Fixit, but Fixit easily got rid of them. He was not so lucky with Frost, whose superhuman strength was comparable to Fixit's, but Fixit intimidated Striker, convincing him to back down. Striker, choosing his battles, decided to retreat and suggested that he had been only offering her help to her widow but, if she didn't want it, he would leave. Fixit's sudden arrival brought attention that Striker wanted for himself, and Striker decided to get rid of Fixit before continuing his plans. At the same time, one of Fixit's men, Paris, who had empathic powers, said he had sensed such happiness and self-satisfaction in Striker during their encounter, that he was convinced that Striker had murdered Berengetti; and Fixit had gone to Las Vegas to solve the murder of his friend

served: Continuity Notes Tales to Astonish Vol 1 49 Continuity Notes This issue clarifies that although Henry Pym spends his crime-fighting time in New York City, his home and laboratory are actually in New Jersey. Ant-Man Scott Lang (Earth-616) Ant-Man When his daughter Cassie was diagnosed as having a serious congenital heart condition, Lang sought the aid of surgeon Dr. Erica Sondheim. Desperate to help his daughter, Lang decided to return to thievery. Breaking into the New Jersey home of Dr. Henry Pym, Lang stole Ant-Man's Suit. Unknown to him, Pym observed the theft and in his guise as Yellowjacket, followed Lang, curious to see what use he would put the paraphernalia. Garbed as Ant-Man, Lang broke into Cross and discovered Dr. Sondheim was held prisoner by Darren Cross, president of CTE, who needed Sondheim to correct his own heart condition. Rescuing Sondheim and defeating Cross, Lang was relieved when Sondheim was able to save the life of his daughter. Lang intended to return the Ant-Man costume to its owner and turn himself in, but Henry Pym offered to let him keep them, provided Lang put them to lawful use. Early Life Henry Pym (Earth-12041) Early Life Henry "Hank" Pym, is an American scientist who discovered a rare group of subatomic particles, which have become known as the "Pym Particles." With them, he began his superhero carrier as the Ant-Man alongside his wife Janet Van Dyne who became known as the Wasp. At some point, he passed on the Ant-Man mantle to Scott Lang. Early Life / Discovering Pym Particles Henry Pym (Earth-616)/Expanded History Early Life / Discovering Pym Particles After many more tests, Pym decided to foolishly test the Pym Particles on himself, shrinking down in size. He was chased out of his home by a mouse, and stumbled down into an anthill while fleeing some ants. Here, accounts of what happened in the ant-hill vary. In one account, Pym fell into a pile of honey and was freed by an ant. The other members of the colony tried to kill him, but he managed to fight them off using a match that he discovered within the tunnels. The helpful ant then assisted him in returning to his home and using the growth formula to restore himself to normal. Another account states that there was no clash with the ants, he only encountered the one empathetic ant - which he named Dusty - who brought him back to the growth formula. When both Pym and Dusty were exposed to the formula, they grew in size. This was a boon to Pym, who could now examine a much larger specimen. He was interrupted by Janet van Dyne who had tracked him down and asked him out to dinner. In order to get rid of her before she saw Dusty, Pym reluctantly agreed. Later, when he had dinner with Janet and her father, he explained his research and, while Vernon was unimpressed, Janet was even more smitten by Pym. The two then began dating while in his spare time, Henry continued to study Dusty and learn how ants communicated with one another. Restoration Henry Pym (Earth-616)

Speaker: The Maker Quotesource: Ultimates 2 Vol 2 9 History: ===Foreword: The Multiversal Cycle=== All of reality has gone through eight different incarnations, each one triggered by a different instance of multiversal renewal, which constitutes in the destruction and re-creation of everything there is. Originally, there was no Multiverse. The First Firmament was a single, eternal, unchanging universe. However, its first beings, the Celestials, shattered it into the first-ever Multiverse, the Second Cosmos. As the Celestials had desired change and evolution, the Multiverse died and was reborn several times, evolving each time. The Third Cosmos introduced narrative; the Fourth, archetypes; the Fifth, magic; and the Sixth, science. In Earth-616's previous incarnation in the Sixth Cosmos, the Paradise-like planet of Taa existed. When the sixth incarnation was destroyed by an entity called the Black Winter, it left an existential void in its wake until the universe was eventually reborn with the Big Bang. The current universe was part of the Seventh Cosmos. It was where Earth existed, protected by super heroes like the Fantastic Four, the Avengers, and the X-Men. However, the Multiverse was destroyed by beings from outside the Multiverse called the Beyonders and the phenomenon known as the incursions. The intervention of Mister Fantastic in the Multiverse's rebirth caused the Eighth Cosmos to be a direct continuation of the Seventh, instead of being a completely new version. After Arthur appeared to abandon his extremist crusade, Eleanor married him, and he adopted her daughter Jenny. For a time, their family life seemed stable, but Eleanor gradually noticed troubling signs that her husband was slipping back into his old obsessions. Her fears intensified when news broke that two petty criminals had been found murdered inside a church, their bodies bearing sword wounds. The police initially suspected the Black Knight, whose weaponry matched the injuries. Recognizing the pattern and fearing the truth, Eleanor went directly to the Black Knight’s residence. There, she revealed that Arthur had recently become consumed again with the Crusader identity and had spoken obsessively about killing someone he referred to as the “Saracen.” Eleanor’s warning proved accurate. With the Emir of Ghulistan scheduled to visit Washington, D.C., Arthur fully reclaimed the Crusader persona and set out to assassinate the Emir, whom he believed to be the Saracen. The night before the Emir’s arrival, the Crusader had murdered the two church thieves, and the following day launched his attack. The Black Knight intervened, but the Crusader initially overpowered him. The confrontation ended only when Jenny appeared, pleading with her stepfather to stop. Her presence broke through Arthur’s fanaticism, allowing him a moment of clarity. Overcome with remorse, he shattered his own sword and shield and surrendered to authorities, leaving Eleanor and Jenny to face the emotional aftermath of his collapse into zealotry. She had an almost obsessive hatred for cockroaches, as well as foreigners, who she blamed for the filth in the city that attracted insects. One night, she awoke from a restless sleep to find her own apartment filled with roaches. In a panic, she screamed at them, telling them to go away, and to her surprise, they obeyed. Testing her powers, she realized she could communicate with the roaches, and ordered them to go to the apartment of her immigrant neighbors and devour them. When she heard the screams, she decided to celebrate with a drink, but found more cockroaches in her cupboard. She realized she could read their thoughts, and that the swarm of roaches were all telling her that they loved her. Oddly touched by the affection, she responded by telling them that she loved them too, and ordered them to come to her. At her command, every roach in the city came towards her, apparently smothering her. She only had time to scream once. Solon Stabilizer's ship landed on Earth in search of indium to repair a damaged solar cell. Unfortunately, Earth's oxygen made her disoriented and she was used by a group of homeless thieves --- who named her Spinnerette --- to rob jewelry stores, mistaking silver for indium. The couple were unable to stop the robberies thanks to Solon's ability to destabilize them with a crushing sense of vertigo. served: Early Life Elizabeth Braddock (Earth-9997) Early Life The early life of Psylocke largely mirrors that of her Earth-616 counterpart. Elizabeth Braddock was the sister of Brian Braddock, who would go on to become Captain Britain. Being a mutant with the powers of telepathy and telekinesis, Elizabeth briefly tried to fill her brother's shoes, but was blinded by one of his foes. She would eventually recover, and became a member of the X-Men. After being gravely wounded in battle against the Adversary, she led them into the Siege Perilous, which healed their wounds. Otherworld Margaret Braddock (Earth-616) Otherworld The family later relocated to Braddock Manor, where Elizabeth briefly joined them. Amid rising anti-mutant sentiment in England and Brian’s disappearance, Meggan moved with Maggie to Krakoa, where she met her uncle Jamie Braddock Jr. After Jamie became king of Avalon and Brian was named Captain Avalon, the family settled in Castle Camelot in Otherworld. Maggie’s intellect continued to flourish, assisting her mother Meggan in her role as court sorceress. Her fae heritage, inherited from Meggan, became more pronounced during their time in Avalon. Maggie frequently used Krakoan gateways to visit Earth, particularly the Braddock Lighthouse, where Excalibur and her aunt Elizabeth resided. Her ability to use the mutant-exclusive gates suggests she is a mutant. Maggie later accompanied her family to the Starlight Citadel to witness Saturnyne’s trial of the false Captains Britain during Avalon’s civil war. Displaying keen strategic skills, she aided her family in war tactics. Despite efforts to evacuate her to Earth for safety, Maggie refused to leave without her mother. When Merlyn’s forces conquered Castle Camelot, the Braddocks escaped to the Braddock Lighthouse. served: Fire and Life Incarnate Jean Grey (Earth-616) Fire and Life Incarnate With her dying breath, Jean Grey called out for aid and the Phoenix Force, which had touched her mind prior, manifested to assist her. Jean was shocked that an omnipotent entity had answered her call, and believed she was going insane in her last moments, to which the Phoenix replied she was no more confused than any finite being experiencing the infinite. The Phoenix explained its consciousness derived from that of Grey, and revealed that she was not dying; she was already dead and only conscious because of the force of her will. Wishing to save the X-Men as well as to live, Jean Grey entered into a communion to the Phoenix, resulting in a complete merger between the two from that moment on. The psychic mutant's very essence, including her form, memories and personality, was transferred to the Phoenix inside the shuttle, as her moribund body collapsed. Intoxicated by experiencing humanity, Phoenix fell under the belief that she was the real Jean Grey, but was startled to see Jean's lifeless body. Noticing a spark of life within it that still fought back, the Phoenix encased the decayed body within an energy cocoon to revive the soul within, while she also feared what would happen when the body was fully rejuvenated. Jean Grey's sacrifice saved the lives of the X-Men, who returned safely to Earth. Upon re-entry, the spacecraft crashed into Jamaica Bay. In a magnificent display of power, following death and resurrection, Phoenix emerged from the sea, introducing herself to the X-Men as a transformed Jean Grey. However, the immense power and new sensations overwhelmed her. Placed under medical treatment, Phoenix recovered and contended with her death and return to life. Dormant at the bottom of the sea, Jean Grey's original body rested in secrecy, while she lived through the cosmic entity who replicated her identity.
